editorial.headline: Fuel Retail at Indonesia’s Filling Stations: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the sale of transport fuel at filling facilities, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity is the retail sale of fuel through filling facilities serving land, sea and air transport. Its reach is broader than the familiar roadside station: it includes petroleum fuel, gaseous fuel, LPG, LNG and other fuel types, including hydrogen, supplied for motor vehicles, speed boats and generators. The setting is the fuel-filling facility itself, whether serving cars and motorcycles or transport beyond the road. In practice, the activity may also sit alongside sales of lubricants, cooling products, cleaning materials and other goods used for cars and motorcycles.

It is an activity open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the description is framed around operating infrastructure and the direct retail supply of fuel, rather than a narrow product category. The business is defined by the point of sale and the transport use it serves: a facility where fuel is made available to vehicles, vessels or generators, with the familiar adjacent range of vehicle-care goods permitted within the same commercial setting.

For foreign investment, the national position is direct. The activity is classified as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA activities classified as Low or Medium-Low risk across the island. This activity is not marked as blocked: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by that moratorium. Bali’s recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For an investor considering a fuel-filling operation in Bali, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: the activity remains open for PMA registration, while the relevant record identifies the Besar-scale activity as carrying a medium-high or high OSS risk classification rather than a moratorium block.
